name: arazoza-formatter
description: Format an Arazoza Brothers takeoff worksheet (.xlsx/.xlsm) into the standard Takeoff Monkey worksheet layout. In a fixed order it: leaves the group headers in 'Description' exactly as written, moves the item names from 'Size' into 'Description', fixes misspelled botanical (Latin) plant names in those item names (only Latin words, only small spelling fixes — group names, common names, cultivars and everything else are never re-spelled), moves the sizing from 'Notes' into 'Size', appends the size to each description with ' - ', sets Size/Package for soil & mulch items that state a depth, normalises UOM values (count/ea/each → Unit, sf → Square Feet, lf → Linear Feet), and copies package types found in Size (FG, cont/container, B&B) into 'Package'. A row where Description and Size were both filled is filled RED and left as it came. Produces a NEW copy of the workbook: the formatted data stays on the worksheet's own sheet (so the ribbon, macros such as Arazoza Export, tables and formulas keep working), and an untouched copy of the original data is added as a '<sheet> (original)' tab. The uploaded file is never modified.
when_to_use: Use when the user says a job or worksheet is an Arazoza project, or when an attached spreadsheet's filename contains 'Arazoza' and they want it formatted, cleaned up, or prepared. Pass the worksheet (.xlsx/.xlsm) as input_file — never a schedule image or PDF. A worksheet MUST be attached: if the user talks about an Arazoza job but no worksheet is attached to this message or earlier in the thread, do not start any work and do not reach for run_code — use ask_user to ask them to upload the Arazoza worksheet first. Its steps must run in a fixed order, so never reproduce or 'finish' them with run_code. Do NOT use for non-Arazoza worksheets, or for pulling schedules out of PDFs (that's schedule-extractor).

input_file.description: Handle of the attached Arazoza worksheet (.xlsx or .xlsm) to format, e.g. "file_1". Must be one of the file handles listed in the conversation, and must be the spreadsheet — not a schedule image.

sheet_name.description: Optional: the sheet to format. Omit it and the tool finds the sheet with the worksheet's 'Description'/'Size' header row itself (the normal case). Only set this if the user named a sheet or the tool reported it couldn't find the table.

force.description: Leave false. The tool refuses a sheet that doesn't look like a raw Arazoza worksheet (nothing in 'Size' to move into 'Description'), because running on an already-formatted sheet would flag every item red. Set true ONLY if the user has explicitly told you to run it anyway.

output: A new copy of the workbook named '<original name> - formatted.<ext>': the worksheet formatted on its own sheet, plus a '<sheet> (original)' tab with the data as it arrived. Everything else in the file (VBA, ribbon, shapes, tables) is carried over unchanged. Also a text summary: which cells were filled red and why, how many group headers were kept, every Latin-name spelling fix (row: before → after) or why that check didn't run, how many items/notes were moved and merged, soil/mulch depth rows, UOM conversions, and packages filled. Red-filled cells always need a human look.
